title: Gaudium IVF and Women Health Ltd - 544709 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Gaudium Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 17.9% YoY to INR37.4 crores, while EBITDA margin fell to 36% from 43.4% on new-hub rollout costs.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 17.9% YoY to INR37.4 crores and H1 grew 14.7% to INR56.8 crores, with the standalone IVF business up 22.3% in Q2. Consolidated EBITDA was flat at INR13.5 crores, but margin contracted 737 bps to 36% as South Extension (Delhi) and Gurgaon were launched and marketing spend was increased. Management says margins at existing hubs are stable and the pressure is expansion-driven. FY27 revenue guidance of INR130 crores is reaffirmed, with H2 expected to be stronger.

segments.name: Mature hubs / core IVF (standalone)
segments.commentary: Standalone IVF revenue grew 22.3% YoY to INR28.1 crores in Q2 and 18.5% to INR41.7 crores in H1. Management cited roughly 28% growth at the core hubs in Mumbai, Delhi and Bangalore, with Patna dragging the blended figure after its relocation.

segments.name: New hubs
segments.commentary: South Extension (Delhi) started 16 July 2026 and has about 15 cycles to date, and is near breakeven at about 2.5 months. Gurgaon (Civil Lines) started 24 September 2026 and has booked its first cycle.

segments.name: Geographic mix
segments.commentary: Delhi contributes about 50% of revenue. Other contributors are Mumbai, Bangalore, Jammu and Kashmir, Ludhiana and Patna.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR130 crores reaffirmed, with H2 expected to be stronger and Q4 the seasonally strongest quarter.
Management aims to hold historical margins by end of FY27 after temporary pressure from new-hub launches and marketing.
Medium-term aspiration of about 25% revenue growth per year, per the Chairperson's confirmation of an analyst's framing; FY28-29 growth expected to be supported by new hubs.

Plan to open 10 centres in FY27: 3 done (South Extension, Gurgaon and Nagpur awaiting approval, which the call treats as the third), with 5 more identified (Lucknow, Kolkata, Guwahati, Surat, Hyderabad). Rollout of remaining hubs over 18-24 months.
Receivables target of about INR10 crores (roughly 20% of revenue) for FY27 per management.
Gaudium Women Hospital in Lucknow approved by the board in June 2026, project cost up to INR15 crores on a 30-year lease, commercialisation expected in FY28-29.
capex_capacity: Capex per new hub about INR2.5 crores, of which INR1.5 crores goes to the lab and OT; target size about 3,000 sq ft.

New hubs expected to break even in about 3-6 months, ramp to 25 cycles in 1-1.5 years, and pay back in about 1.5-2 years. Stabilised revenue is INR0.6-1 crore for a Tier 2 hub and INR1.5-2 crores for a metro hub.
Existing hubs can handle up to about 120 cycles with current infrastructure. Mumbai does 50-70 cycles a month, Bangalore 30-40 and Kashmir about 25. Metro hubs are considered strong above 75 cycles.
Q2 saw 889 pickup cycles across the network (each generally followed by an embryo transfer).
Network at 30 Sep 2026: 9 hubs and 38 spokes, after 4 spokes added around South Extension and 3 around Gurgaon.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is still rising at existing centres and new centres are seeing footfalls. South Extension has about 15 cycles to date.
Medical tourism expected to be strong in December, with patients from more than 30 countries. Hyderabad planned to draw Middle East tourism and Kolkata planned to draw Bangladesh tourism.
Volume-led growth is larger than price-led growth; management said price differences are not large.
Management said it is deliberately shifting marketing to tap untapped markets rather than only the existing ~22% growth segment, which raised marketing spend.
A private insurer has launched a three-cycle package with Gaudium, described as a first for the company. Management cited an 85% cumulative pregnancy rate.
Clinical outcomes: first-attempt clinical pregnancy rate is 62%, up from 56% before the AI tools SiD and ERICA were introduced.
Deferred payment plans: Q2 direct credit business was about INR60-80 lakhs. About INR4 crores came through an aggregator working with about 10 NBFCs.

qa_highlights.question: How is Q3 IVF demand and medical tourism looking?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand is still rising at existing centres and new centres are getting footfalls. Management expects December to be a strong medical tourism month, with patients from more than 30 countries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth in the core seven hubs in H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the existing centres grew roughly 28%. The blended standalone growth was lower because Patna was relocated and operations were paused during the move.

qa_highlights.question: What are the revenue growth aspirations for FY28 and FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth has historically been over 30% YoY and it is confident of continuing with new hubs. The analyst's framing of about 25% was accepted as fair.

qa_highlights.question: Is there room to grow existing hubs without capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current hubs can reach about 120 cycles without extension. The analyst's view that revenue could double or rise 70-80% without capex was agreed.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex, breakeven, payback and stabilised revenue per new hub?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR2.5 crores per hub, with breakeven in 3-6 months and payback in 1.5-2 years. Stabilised revenue is INR0.6-1 crore for Tier 2 and INR1.5-2 crores for metros.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state ROE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said historical ROE is about 52%, and it expects a similar level once all hubs are running and revenue has ramped.

qa_highlights.question: What are the receivables and why are receivable days high at 165?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone receivables were INR32.83 crores on 30 Sep 2026 against INR42.6 crores on 31 Mar 2026. Consolidated was INR45.30 crores against INR53.37 crores. Clinical cases where egg collection precedes treatment and deferred payment plans for financial reasons explain the high days. The company targets about INR10 crores by year end.

qa_highlights.question: Will new-hub marketing and salary costs keep margins under pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins to be maintained by year end. Doctor and embryologist salaries start a month before launch, so some temporary pressure is expected until the hubs mature.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company position itself in Kolkata against Nova, Renew and Neotia?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to clinical expertise, Gaudium Signature Lab with AI tools, a doctor-led SOP approach built over 17 years, and existing Kolkata patients who travel to Delhi.

risks_watch: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 36% in Q2 and 28% in H1, versus 43.4% and 38.3% a year earlier; management expects recovery only by year end.
Receivable days of 165 and consolidated receivables of INR45.3 crores. Recovery depends on deferred-payment and NBFC/aggregator channels.
Pre-launch salary overlap and marketing spend in each new hub, with rollout continuing over 18-24 months.
Nagpur hub is ready but awaiting regulatory approval, which could delay the 10-centre FY27 target.
Rising competition, which management acknowledged in its FY28-29 growth outlook.
Clinical outcome claims (62% first-attempt rate, 85% cumulative rate) are management-reported and not independently verified in the call.
Patna relocation temporarily halted operations, and the core-hub growth figure of 28% excludes Patna.
key_quotes: The pressure on reported margins comes from expansion, not from the core business.
So our estimate is by the end of the year we will be able to maintain the historical margins.
Historically it's around 52%. So probably we might end up around the same number once all the hubs are started and revenue starts kicking in.
So if 10 couples walk into Gaudium, 8.5 are likely to go back pregnant.
summary.management_tone: Confident on clinical outcomes, demand and the core IVF business, saying existing-hub margins are stable and recovery is expected by year end. Cautious and sometimes evasive on margin pressure, receivable days at 165, and the details of Patna and the capacity and revenue-per-hub answers, which management gave only loosely.

adds.what: South Extension (Delhi) IVF hub, started 16 July 2026
Gurgaon (Civil Lines) IVF hub, started 24 September 2026
Nagpur hub, awaiting approval (third of 10 FY27 centres)
Gaudium Women Hospital, Lucknow (30-year lease, project cost up to INR15 crores)
Five further FY27 centres identified (Lucknow, Kolkata, Guwahati, Surat, Hyderabad), rollout over 18-24 months

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance of INR130 crores is reaffirmed (implies about 30% growth on the brief's figures, though H1 grew only 14.7%, so H2 must accelerate sharply); backing is partial, with two new hubs live, Nagpur approved, five more identified, and a ~25% medium-term aspiration that is not tied to specific orders.

quality.why: Consolidated revenue rose 17.9% in Q2 (INR37.4 cr vs INR31.7 cr) and management says volume-led growth is larger than price-led, with core hubs up about 28% and new hubs starting from scratch; the brief flags no one-off gains, losses, or weak year-ago base, and the margin squeeze is from new-hub costs rather than growth quality.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects to restore historical margins by year end after new-hub salaries and marketing; consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 36% in Q2 from 43.4% and 28% in H1, but existing-hub margins are described as stable.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Nine hubs and 38 spokes live at 30 Sep 2026 with South Extension (16 Jul) and Gurgaon (24 Sep) commissioned, Nagpur approved, and 10 FY27 centres targeted (3 done, 5 identified) with rollout over 18-24 months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Demand is rising at existing centres (standalone IVF +22.3% in Q2, core hubs ~28%) and 889 pickup cycles in Q2, but H1 consolidated growth was only 14.7% against FY27 guidance of INR130 crores that implies about 30%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Five further FY27 centres (Lucknow, Kolkata, Guwahati, Surat, Hyderabad) are identified and rollout continues over 18-24 months at about INR2.5 crores per hub, with Lucknow women hospital already board-approved at up to INR15 crores; existing hubs can only go to about 120 cycles, so further capex is needed beyond that.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance of INR130 crores was only reaffirmed, not raised, and H1 revenue of INR56.8 crores grew just 14.7%, so H2 needs to be far stronger to hit the target.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 must deliver roughly INR73 crores against INR56.8 crores in H1 to reach INR130 crores, and the Nagpur approval and new-hub ramp could slip; management also acknowledged rising competition.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Three-cycle insurer package launched and medical tourism push into Hyderabad (Middle East) and Kolkata (Bangladesh) planned, but no new product or molecule launch date was given.

rows.label: Medical tourism surge in December
rows.why: Management expects December to be strong with patients from more than 30 countries, and Q2 pickup cycles were 889.

rows.label: Receivables cut to about INR10 crores
rows.why: Consolidated receivables were INR45.3 crores at 165 days on 30 Sep 2026 against a target of about INR10 crores (roughly 20% of revenue), with reliance on deferred-payment and NBFC channels that are not yet proven.

rows.label: Patna relocation restart
rows.why: Patna operations were paused during the relocation and dragged blended standalone growth below the ~28% core-hub rate, with no restart figures given.

tone.note: Management was confident on clinical outcomes, demand and the core IVF business, and on recovering margins by year end. It was cautious on margin pressure, 165 receivable days, Patna and the per-hub revenue answers; analysts pushed on growth aspirations, ROE and capacity headroom.
